quests.instruction: Which part of a vehicle stores the gasoline or fuel it needs to run?
quests.hint: Think about the part hidden inside a car that holds the gasoline before it reaches the engine.
quests.explanation: A fuel tank is a part that stores gasoline. Vehicles use fuel from the tank to power their engine!
quests.funFact: A full fuel tank can help a car travel hundreds of miles before it needs to be refilled!

quests.instruction: Which panel in front of the driver's seat shows speed, fuel level, and other important information?
quests.hint: Think about the panel right behind the steering wheel, full of dials and lights showing important information.
quests.explanation: A dashboard is a panel showing important information. Drivers glance at the dashboard to check their speed and fuel!
quests.funFact: A dashboard uses simple symbols and lights so a driver can understand it with just a quick glance!

quests.instruction: Which round rubber part wraps around a wheel and touches the road?
quests.hint: Think about the black rubber part that wraps around a wheel and grips the road as a car drives.
quests.explanation: A tire is a rubber part that wraps around a wheel. Tires grip the road to help a vehicle move safely!
quests.funFact: Tires are filled with air, which helps them grip the road and cushion every bump!

quests.instruction: Which looping metal links connect a bicycle's pedals to its back wheel?
quests.hint: Think about the looping metal links that connect a bicycle's pedals to the back wheel, making it spin.
quests.explanation: A chain is a looping metal part connecting pedals to a wheel. Pedaling moves the chain, which turns the wheel!
quests.funFact: Oiling a bicycle chain regularly helps it turn smoothly without squeaking!

quests.instruction: Which small metal leg swings down to hold a parked bicycle upright?
quests.hint: Think about the small metal leg you flip down with your foot to keep a bicycle standing up on its own.
quests.explanation: A kickstand is a small leg that holds a bicycle upright. Flipping down the kickstand lets a bike stand alone!
quests.funFact: A kickstand lets you park your bicycle without needing to lean it against something else!

quests.instruction: Which container attaches to the front of a bicycle to carry small items?
quests.hint: Think about the woven container attached to the front of a bicycle, perfect for carrying a small bag.
quests.explanation: A basket is a container attached to a bicycle. Riders carry small items, like groceries, in a basket!
quests.funFact: A bicycle basket makes it easy to carry a book, snack, or small bag along on your ride!

quests.instruction: Which curved cover sits above a wheel to block splashing mud and water?
quests.hint: Think about the curved cover arching over a bicycle wheel that keeps muddy water from splashing you.
quests.explanation: A fender is a curved cover above a wheel. Fenders block splashing mud and water while you ride!
quests.funFact: Riding in the rain is much less splashy for a cyclist whose bicycle has fenders!

quests.instruction: Which thin metal rod connects the center of a wheel to its outer rim?
quests.hint: Think about the thin metal rods you can see crisscrossing between the center and the edge of a bicycle wheel.
quests.explanation: A spoke is a thin rod connecting a wheel's center to its rim. Many spokes together keep a wheel strong and round!
quests.funFact: A single bicycle wheel usually has dozens of thin spokes holding its round shape!

quests.instruction: Which part of a car's exhaust system helps make the engine sound quieter?
quests.hint: Think about the part underneath a car that helps soften the loud rumble of the engine.
quests.explanation: A muffler is a part that makes an engine quieter. Mufflers help soften the loud sound of an engine!
quests.funFact: Without a muffler, a car's engine would sound much louder and noisier on the road!

quests.instruction: Which part of a car do you turn with a key to start the engine?
quests.hint: Think about the small slot near the steering wheel where you turn a key to start the whole car.
quests.explanation: An ignition is a part you turn with a key to start a car. Turning the ignition wakes up the engine!
quests.funFact: Many newer cars now start with the simple push of a button instead of turning a key!

quests.instruction: Which pedal helps a driver smoothly switch gears in certain cars?
quests.hint: Think about the extra pedal on the left side, pressed with your foot whenever you switch gears.
quests.explanation: A clutch is a pedal that helps switch gears smoothly. Drivers press the clutch before changing gears!
quests.funFact: Learning to smoothly use a clutch pedal takes new drivers quite a bit of careful practice!

quests.instruction: Which pedal does a driver press with their foot to make a car go faster?
quests.hint: Think about the pedal on the right side that a driver presses down to speed the car up.
quests.explanation: An accelerator is a pedal that makes a car go faster. Pressing the accelerator gently speeds up the engine!
quests.funFact: Pressing the accelerator smoothly and gently helps make a car ride feel nice and comfortable!

quests.instruction: Which gauge on a dashboard shows the total distance a vehicle has ever traveled?
quests.hint: Think about the numbers on the dashboard that show exactly how many miles a car has driven in its whole life.
quests.explanation: An odometer is a gauge showing total distance traveled. The odometer's numbers slowly climb higher every trip!
quests.funFact: A car's odometer keeps counting up every single mile, even after many, many years of driving!

quests.instruction: Which gauge on a dashboard shows exactly how fast a vehicle is going right now?
quests.hint: Think about the dial on the dashboard with a needle that points to show how fast the car is moving right now.
quests.explanation: A speedometer is a gauge showing current speed. Drivers glance at the speedometer to stay within the speed limit!
quests.funFact: A speedometer's needle moves up and down instantly as a car speeds up or slows down!

quests.instruction: Which blinking light tells other drivers which way a car is about to turn?
quests.hint: Think about the blinking light a driver switches on to warn others before turning left or right.
quests.explanation: A turn signal is a blinking light showing a planned turn. Drivers switch on a turn signal before changing direction!
quests.funFact: Using a turn signal early gives other drivers plenty of time to notice and react safely!

quests.instruction: Which thin blade sweeps back and forth across the glass to clear away rain?
quests.hint: Think about the thin blade that swishes back and forth across the front glass during a rainy drive.
quests.explanation: A windshield wiper is a blade that clears rain from the glass. Wipers sweep back and forth to keep the view clear!
quests.funFact: Windshield wipers can move faster or slower depending on how hard the rain is falling!

quests.instruction: Which pedal do you press with your foot to make a car speed up?
quests.hint: Think about the pedal under your right foot that makes the whole car speed up when you press it.
quests.explanation: A gas pedal is a pedal that speeds up a car. Pressing the gas pedal gives the engine more power!
quests.funFact: A light, gentle press on the gas pedal helps a car speed up smoothly and safely!

quests.instruction: Which dial on a dashboard shows how much fuel is left in the tank?
quests.hint: Think about the little dial on the dashboard with a needle showing whether the tank is full or almost empty.
quests.explanation: A fuel gauge is a dial showing how much fuel remains. Drivers check the fuel gauge before a long trip!
quests.funFact: A fuel gauge helps remind a driver exactly when it's time to stop for more fuel!

quests.instruction: Which sturdy frame on top of a car carries extra luggage or bicycles?
quests.hint: Think about the sturdy metal frame fixed to the top of a car, used to carry bikes or extra bags.
quests.explanation: A roof rack is a frame on top of a car for extra cargo. Families use a roof rack for extra bikes or luggage!
quests.funFact: A roof rack gives a car much more room to carry bulky things like bicycles or kayaks!

quests.instruction: Which storage area inside a ship or airplane carries boxes and luggage?
quests.hint: Think about the large storage space deep inside a ship or plane where all the luggage is packed.
quests.explanation: A cargo hold is a storage area for boxes and luggage. Ships and airplanes both have a cargo hold!
quests.funFact: Workers carefully load a cargo hold to keep the whole ship or airplane balanced evenly!

quests.instruction: Which small, round window lets light into the cabin of a ship?
quests.hint: Think about the small, round window on the side of a ship, letting a little sunlight into the cabin.
quests.explanation: A porthole is a small, round window on a ship. Portholes let light into a ship's cabin!
quests.funFact: A porthole's round shape and thick glass help it stay strong against powerful ocean waves!

quests.instruction: Which narrow board or ramp lets passengers walk safely from the dock onto a ship?
quests.hint: Think about the narrow ramp passengers walk across to step safely from the dock onto a big ship.
quests.explanation: A gangplank is a narrow ramp for boarding a ship. Passengers walk across the gangplank to get on board!
quests.funFact: A gangplank often has railings on each side to help keep boarding passengers extra safe!

quests.instruction: Which long, sturdy part runs along the very bottom of a boat to keep it steady?
quests.hint: Think about the long, hidden part running underneath a sailboat that keeps it from tipping over.
quests.explanation: A keel is a sturdy part along the bottom of a boat. The keel helps keep a boat steady and balanced!
quests.funFact: A keel acts like a boat's spine, giving the whole hull its strength and shape!

quests.instruction: Which pointed front end of a boat cuts through the water first?
quests.hint: Think about the very front, pointed end of a boat that slices through the waves first.
quests.explanation: A bow is the pointed front end of a boat. The bow cuts through the water as a boat moves forward!
quests.funFact: A pointed bow helps a boat slice smoothly through waves instead of pushing straight into them!

quests.instruction: Which back end of a boat is opposite the pointed front?
quests.hint: Think about the flatter back end of a boat, the part farthest from the pointed front.
quests.explanation: A stern is the back end of a boat. The stern is the opposite end from the pointed bow!
quests.funFact: A boat's rudder is usually attached right at the stern, helping steer the whole boat!

quests.instruction: Which wheeled part folds down from an airplane so it can safely touch the runway?
quests.hint: Think about the wheels that fold down from underneath an airplane just before it touches the runway.
quests.explanation: Landing gear is the wheeled part that lets a plane touch down. Landing gear folds down before landing!
quests.funFact: Landing gear folds neatly up inside the airplane once it is safely flying through the sky!

quests.instruction: Which long, tube-shaped main body of an airplane holds the passengers and cargo?
quests.hint: Think about the long, tube-shaped middle part of an airplane where all the passenger seats are found.
quests.explanation: A fuselage is the long, tube-shaped body of an airplane. Passengers and cargo ride inside the fuselage!
quests.funFact: An airplane's fuselage is built extra strong and round to handle high pressure while flying!

quests.instruction: Which front area of a large airplane holds the pilot's seat and flight controls?
quests.hint: Think about the front section of a big airplane, filled with screens and switches for the pilot to use.
quests.explanation: A flight deck is the front area with a pilot's controls. Large airplanes call their cockpit a flight deck!
quests.funFact: A flight deck is filled with careful checklists that pilots follow before every single flight!

quests.instruction: Which small car rides at the very back of an old-fashioned freight train?
quests.hint: Think about the small, often red car that used to ride at the very end of a long freight train.
quests.explanation: A caboose is a small car at the back of a train. Cabooses once let crew members watch the whole train!
quests.funFact: A caboose often had a little lookout window on top so crew members could check the whole train!

quests.instruction: Which slatted opening at the front of a car lets cool air reach the engine?
quests.hint: Think about the slatted opening at the very front of a car, right below the headlights, letting air flow in.
quests.explanation: A grille is a slatted opening at the front of a car. The grille lets cool air flow in to the engine!
quests.funFact: A car's grille shape often helps give that particular car its own unique look!
